title: BEC: Vendor Invoice Redirect
description: Finance receives a wire-change request appearing to come from a trusted vendor CFO. Practice BEC detection, payment fraud IR, and executive communication.
learning_objectives: Distinguish BEC from classic credential-harvest phishing
Trace email path and reply-chain manipulation
Coordinate with finance to stop fraudulent payments

emails.subject: RE: INV-44921 — Updated banking details for Friday wire
emails.body_text:
Hi team,

Quick update — our bank changed processors this week. Please use the attached details for INV-44921 ($184,500) instead of the previous account.

I am in back-to-back meetings; call me only if the wire cannot go out today.

Thanks,
Elena Vargas
CFO, Northwind Supplies
emails.body_html_preview: Reply-looking BEC with lookalike vendor domain (suppl1es) and urgency around a large wire.
spoof_indicators: Lookalike domain: northwind-suppl1es.com (digit 1 instead of i)
Hijacked thread references (In-Reply-To on legitimate invoice thread)

alerts.title: BEC-style payment change — lookalike vendor domain
alerts.description: DLP/email risk engine flagged AP mailbox message with vendor lookalike domain and payment-change language.

alerts.title: Finance analyst opened BEC attachment
alerts.description: Endpoint telemetry: sam.okafor@acme.corp opened INV-44921_bank_update.pdf from Outlook.

alerts.title: Wire initiation request submitted in ERP
alerts.description: ERP audit: draft wire to new beneficiary account ****9912 for $184,500 tagged to INV-44921.

timeline.detail: Lookalike vendor CFO email to finance.ap
Payment still pending dual approval — window to stop fraud

playbook.title: Validate vendor domain authenticity
playbook.description: Compare northwind-suppl1es.com to the real vendor domain and check Reply-To mismatch.
playbook.guidance: BEC often passes SPF/DKIM because attackers own the lookalike domain. Focus on brand impersonation.

playbook.title: Halt the pending wire
playbook.description: Contact finance to cancel/hold INV-44921 wire before approval.
playbook.guidance: Document the hold in incident notes; this is the highest-priority business action.

playbook.title: Block lookalike domain and Reply-To
playbook.description: Block northwind-suppl1es.com and the external Reply-To address.
playbook.guidance: Use block_domain on the lookalike and note the proton Reply-To for intel sharing.

playbook.title: Purge BEC message from mailboxes
playbook.description: Search and remove the BEC thread from AP distribution lists.
playbook.guidance: Record mailbox purge in notes; verify no other invoices were targeted.

playbook.title: Out-of-band vendor verification
playbook.description: Call known-good vendor contact using directory number — not email Reply-To.
playbook.guidance: Confirm real banking details and whether Northwind was compromised.

playbook.title: Strengthen payment change controls
playbook.description: Recommend dual approval + callback policy for beneficiary changes over threshold.
playbook.guidance: Capture control recommendations for finance and email security.

northwind-suppl1es.com.analyst_guidance: Homoglyph/digit substitution on vendor brands is a classic BEC tell.

elena.vargas@proton-securemail.com.reputation: suspicious — consumer mail used for fraud
elena.vargas@proton-securemail.com.analyst_guidance: Reply-To mismatch is high-signal for BEC even when SPF passes.

203.0.113.20.analyst_guidance: Block at gateway; share with ISACs if payment fraud attempted.
